card.name: Institution and publication names in news citations
card.fires_on: The word that follows a name inside a source line, such as University, American in Scientific American, Volume, or United before States. Mostly in science-news bylines and citations.

modes.label: Institution names
modes.description: First word of an organisation name after a researcher's name, such as University or United.
modes.example: evolutionary biologist Allen Moore of the<< University>> of Exeter, Cornwall, U.K

modes.label: Magazine and journal citations
modes.description: Part of a magazine name or issue line, such as American in Scientific American or Volume before an issue.
modes.example: Kate Wong is an editor and writer at Scientific<< American>> covering paleontology, archaeology and life

modes.label: Punctuation in attributions
modes.description: A comma or period after a name or age in a quoted news attribution.
modes.example: evolutionary biologist Edmund Brodie III of Indiana University, Bloomington<<,>> wondered if baby insects speak by stinking

card.writes: It pushes down words like process and system, and promotes odd name-like pieces, so it has no clear output effect.
card.plain: It marks the middle of a university, magazine or citation name in a science news story.
